title: Grouping with tests and ranking in products

steps.title: category_id with at least 1 rows
steps.prompt:
HAVING can hold any test about the piles.
Here we keep only piles with count(*) >= 1.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING count(*) >= 1;
hints: Write: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING count(*) >= 1;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING count(*) >= 1;

steps.title: Groups ranked by sum(id)
steps.prompt:
You can sort by a total, not just a column.
ORDER BY sum(id) DESC puts the biggest pile-total first.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT category_id, sum(id) FROM products GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY sum(id) DESC;
hints: Write: SELECT category_id, sum(id) FROM products GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY sum(id) DESC;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, sum(id) FROM products GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY sum(id) DESC;
steps.memory_trick: You may sort by an aggregate you computed.
